content.text:
No, it isn't. `src/services/user-service.js` still uses the old callback style. It imports `query` and `update` straight from `../db.js` and writes the queries inline in all three functions (`listActiveUsers`, `findUser`, `softDeleteUser`). A comment at `src/services/user-service.js:3` says so too: *"Callback-style database access. Chapter 5 migrates this to UserRepository."*

`UserRepository` (`src/repositories/user-repository.js`) already has a promise-based method for each of those functions:

| user-service.js (current) | UserRepository equivalent |
|---|---|
| `listActiveUsers(callback)` | `findActive()` |
| `findUser(id, callback)` | `findById(id)` |
| `softDeleteUser(id, when, callback)` | `softDelete(id, when)` |

The project has a `migrate-module` skill for exactly this. It moves one service file onto its repository and runs that module's tests. Moving to promises changes how anything that calls these functions has to use them, so I haven't started it. Want me to run it on `user-service.js`?
